question: The most common type of breech presentation is:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Complete breech (hips and knees flexed) accounts for ~10% of breech cases.
explanations.B: Frank breech is the most common type (~60-70%), with hips flexed and knees extended so feet are near the head.
explanations.C: Footling breech (one or both feet presenting) is less common and high-risk for cord prolapse.
explanations.D: Kneeling breech is the rarest variant.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e — Obstetric Management
explanation: Frank breech is the most common type (~60-70%), with hips flexed and knees extended so feet are near the head.

question: Normal range of central venous pressure (CVP) is:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Too low; would indicate severe hypovolemia.
explanations.B: Normal CVP is 2-6 cm H2O (or 2-8 mmHg depending on reference); reflects right atrial pressure.
explanations.C: Elevated CVP, suggests fluid overload or right heart failure.
explanations.D: Markedly elevated; seen in cardiac tamponade or severe RV failure.

citation: Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing
explanation: Normal CVP is 2-6 cm H2O (or 2-8 mmHg depending on reference); reflects right atrial pressure.

question: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
subject: Nutrition

explanations.A: Vitamin A (retinol) is essential for rhodopsin synthesis in rod cells; deficiency causes nyctalopia (night blindness).
explanations.B: B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and neuropathy.
explanations.C: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.
explanations.D: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia.

citation: ICMR-NIN Nutrient Requirements for Indians; Srilakshmi Dietetics 8e
explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is essential for rhodopsin synthesis in rod cells; deficiency causes nyctalopia (night blindness).

question: The drug of choice for status epilepticus is:
subject: Pharmacology

explanations.A: Phenytoin is second-line after benzodiazepines fail.
explanations.B: IV Lorazepam is the first-line drug of choice for status epilepticus per current guidelines (longer duration than diazepam).
explanations.C: Phenobarbitone is third-line.
explanations.D: Diazepam works but has shorter duration; lorazepam is preferred.

citation: KDT Essentials of Medical Pharmacology 8e
explanation: IV Lorazepam is the first-line drug of choice for status epilepticus per current guidelines (longer duration than diazepam).

question: Normal fetal heart rate is:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Below normal range; suggests bradycardia.
explanations.B: Normal FHR baseline is 110-160 bpm.
explanations.C: Tachycardia; may indicate fetal distress or maternal fever.
explanations.D: Severe bradycardia; emergency.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e — Obstetric Management
explanation: Normal FHR baseline is 110-160 bpm.

question: Which of the following is NOT a part of APGAR score?
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: Heart rate is one of the 5 APGAR components.
explanations.B: Respiratory effort is part of APGAR.
explanations.C: Birth weight is NOT part of APGAR; the 5 are Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration.
explanations.D: Muscle tone (Activity) is part of APGAR.

citation: AAP/AHA Neonatal Resuscitation Program 8e — Delivery Room Management
explanation: Birth weight is NOT part of APGAR; the 5 are Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration.

question: Pulse Polio Immunization in India is given to children up to:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Routine OPV is given in infancy but PPI extends beyond.
explanations.B: Not the cutoff for PPI.
explanations.C: Pulse Polio Immunization targets all children 0 to 5 years.
explanations.D: Beyond the PPI age range.

citation: MoHFW Universal Immunisation Programme — National Immunisation Schedule
explanation: Pulse Polio Immunization targets all children 0 to 5 years.

question: ORS (WHO formula) contains how much sodium per litre?
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: Too low; this is closer to maintenance solutions.
explanations.B: WHO low-osmolarity ORS contains 75 mmol/L sodium (total osmolarity 245 mOsm/L).
explanations.C: This was the older WHO ORS formula (pre-2002).
explanations.D: Too high; would be hypertonic.

citation: Ghai Essential Pediatrics 9e — Growth, Development and Neonatology
explanation: WHO low-osmolarity ORS contains 75 mmol/L sodium (total osmolarity 245 mOsm/L).

question: Which chamber of the heart has the thickest myocardium?
subject: Anatomy

explanations.A: Atria have thin walls.
explanations.B: Left atrium wall is slightly thicker than right but still thin.
explanations.C: Right ventricle is thinner because it pumps to the low-pressure pulmonary circuit.
explanations.D: Left ventricle has the thickest myocardium because it pumps blood against high systemic pressure.

citation: Gray’s Anatomy for Students 4e; Guyton & Hall 14e
explanation: Left ventricle has the thickest myocardium because it pumps blood against high systemic pressure.

question: Mantoux test is read after:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Too early; induration may not have developed.
explanations.B: Mantoux (tuberculin) test is read 48-72 hours after intradermal injection of PPD.
explanations.C: Too late; reaction begins to fade.
explanations.D: Not appropriate timing.

citation: MoHFW National TB Elimination Programme — Technical and Operational Guidelines
explanation: Mantoux (tuberculin) test is read 48-72 hours after intradermal injection of PPD.

question: The most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage is:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Retained tissue is one of the 4 Ts but not the most common.
explanations.B: Uterine atony (Tone) accounts for ~70-80% of PPH cases.
explanations.C: Trauma (lacerations) is second most common.
explanations.D: Thrombin (coagulopathy) is the least common cause.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e / Gynecology 8e
explanation: Uterine atony (Tone) accounts for ~70-80% of PPH cases.

question: BCG vaccine is given by which route?
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: IM route used for DPT, Hep B; not BCG.
explanations.B: Subcutaneous used for measles, MMR; not BCG.
explanations.C: BCG is given intradermally over the left deltoid, dose 0.1 mL (0.05 mL for newborn <1 month).
explanations.D: OPV is oral; BCG is not.

citation: MoHFW Universal Immunisation Programme — National Immunisation Schedule
explanation: BCG is given intradermally over the left deltoid, dose 0.1 mL (0.05 mL for newborn <1 month).

question: Which type of insulin has the most rapid onset of action?
subject: Pharmacology

explanations.A: Regular (short-acting) onset 30 min.
explanations.B: NPH is intermediate-acting, onset 1-2 hours.
explanations.C: Lispro is rapid-acting analog, onset 5-15 minutes.
explanations.D: Glargine is long-acting basal insulin with onset ~1-2 hours but no peak.

citation: KDT Essentials of Medical Pharmacology 8e
explanation: Lispro is rapid-acting analog, onset 5-15 minutes.

question: Compression-to-ventilation ratio in adult CPR (single rescuer) is:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: 15:2 is used for two-rescuer pediatric CPR.
explanations.B: 30:2 is the standard adult CPR ratio (single or two rescuer) per AHA 2020 guidelines.
explanations.C: 5:1 was an old guideline, no longer recommended.
explanations.D: Not a current recommended ratio.

citation: AHA Guidelines 2020 for CPR and ECC — Basic and Advanced Life Support
explanation: 30:2 is the standard adult CPR ratio (single or two rescuer) per AHA 2020 guidelines.

question: First sign of magnesium sulphate toxicity is:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Loss of patellar/deep tendon reflexes is the earliest clinical sign of MgSO4 toxicity (8-10 mEq/L).
explanations.B: Respiratory depression occurs at higher levels (10-15 mEq/L).
explanations.C: Cardiac arrest is the terminal event at very high levels (>25 mEq/L).
explanations.D: Hypotension may occur but is not the earliest specific sign.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e — Obstetric Management
explanation: Loss of patellar/deep tendon reflexes is the earliest clinical sign of MgSO4 toxicity (8-10 mEq/L).

question: Glasgow Coma Scale lowest possible score is:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: GCS minimum is not 0; each component scores at least 1.
explanations.B: Single component minimum, but total minimum is 3.
explanations.C: GCS minimum total is 3 (1 each for eye, verbal, motor); maximum is 15.
explanations.D: Not the minimum total.

citation: Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing
explanation: GCS minimum total is 3 (1 each for eye, verbal, motor); maximum is 15.

question: Most common organism causing neonatal sepsis in India is:
subject: Pediatric

explanations.A: E. coli is common globally but Klebsiella predominates in Indian NICUs.
explanations.B: In India, Klebsiella pneumoniae is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis (NNPD data).
explanations.C: GBS is leading cause in Western countries, less common in India.
explanations.D: Staph aureus is more common in late-onset hospital-acquired sepsis.

citation: Ghai Essential Pediatrics 9e — Growth, Development and Neonatology
explanation: In India, Klebsiella pneumoniae is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis (NNPD data).

question: Which valve is between right atrium and right ventricle?
subject: Anatomy

explanations.A: Mitral (bicuspid) valve lies between left atrium and left ventricle.
explanations.B: Tricuspid valve lies between right atrium and right ventricle.
explanations.C: Pulmonary valve is at exit of right ventricle to pulmonary artery.
explanations.D: Aortic valve is at exit of left ventricle to aorta.

citation: Gray’s Anatomy for Students 4e; Guyton & Hall 14e
explanation: Tricuspid valve lies between right atrium and right ventricle.

question: Korotkoff sounds are heard during measurement of:
subject: Fundamentals

explanations.A: Pulse is palpated, not auscultated for Korotkoff.
explanations.B: Respiratory rate is observed visually.
explanations.C: Korotkoff sounds (5 phases) are heard during auscultatory BP measurement; phase I = systolic, phase V = diastolic.
explanations.D: Temperature uses a thermometer.

citation: Potter & Perry Fundamentals of Nursing 10e
explanation: Korotkoff sounds (5 phases) are heard during auscultatory BP measurement; phase I = systolic, phase V = diastolic.

question: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) was launched in which year?
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Not the launch year.
explanations.B: JSY was launched on 12 April 2005 under NRHM to promote institutional deliveries.
explanations.C: JSSK was launched in 2011, not JSY.
explanations.D: Not correct.

explanation: JSY was launched on 12 April 2005 under NRHM to promote institutional deliveries.

question: Universal donor blood group is:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Has A antigen; not universal.
explanations.B: Has B antigen; not universal.
explanations.C: AB positive is the universal recipient, not donor.
explanations.D: O negative has no A, B, or Rh antigens, hence universal donor for packed RBCs.

citation: Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing
explanation: O negative has no A, B, or Rh antigens, hence universal donor for packed RBCs.

question: First-line antitubercular drug that causes peripheral neuropathy is:
subject: Pharmacology

explanations.A: Rifampicin causes orange discoloration of secretions and hepatotoxicity.
explanations.B: Isoniazid (INH) causes pyridoxine (B6) deficiency leading to peripheral neuropathy; supplement B6 to prevent.
explanations.C: Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricemia and hepatotoxicity.
explanations.D: Ethambutol causes optic neuritis.

citation: KDT Essentials of Medical Pharmacology 8e
explanation: Isoniazid (INH) causes pyridoxine (B6) deficiency leading to peripheral neuropathy; supplement B6 to prevent.

question: Erikson's stage of 'Trust vs Mistrust' occurs at age:
subject: Psychiatric

explanations.A: Trust vs Mistrust is the first Eriksonian stage (infancy, 0-1 year).
explanations.B: 1-3 years is Autonomy vs Shame and Doubt.
explanations.C: 3-6 years is Initiative vs Guilt.
explanations.D: 6-12 years is Industry vs Inferiority.

explanation: Trust vs Mistrust is the first Eriksonian stage (infancy, 0-1 year).

question: Largest artery in the human body is:
subject: Anatomy

explanations.A: Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood; smaller than aorta.
explanations.B: The aorta is the largest artery, originating from the left ventricle.
explanations.C: Carotid is a major branch but not the largest.
explanations.D: Femoral is large but smaller than aorta.

citation: Gray’s Anatomy for Students 4e; Guyton & Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology 14e
explanation: The aorta is the largest artery, originating from the left ventricle.

question: Which is the protein-energy malnutrition disorder characterized by edema?
subject: Nutrition

explanations.A: Marasmus is severe wasting without edema, due to overall calorie deficiency.
explanations.B: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency presenting with bilateral pitting edema, hair changes, hepatomegaly.
explanations.C: Mixed picture has both wasting and edema.
explanations.D: Cachexia is wasting due to chronic disease, not specifically a PEM category.

citation: ICMR-NIN Nutrient Requirements for Indians; Srilakshmi Dietetics 8e
explanation: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency presenting with bilateral pitting edema, hair changes, hepatomegaly.
